audit.why: Gwen 1 through first item, Nasus at 2+ items, matching the 55.38% win rate, the spikes, and the mirror audit at audits/top/nasus__gwen.json which sets his 2+ items stage to Nasus.

audit.whatIsWrong: Wither is called 'his only real threat' and 'bait it' three times with no cooldown, and Fury of the Sands has none either.
audit.why: Wither is 15/14/13/12/11s, so a baited Wither at rank 1 gives you fifteen seconds of full attack speed — that is the whole mid-game window. Fury of the Sands is 120/100/80s and Spirit Fire a flat 12s.
audit.corrected: Numbers added to the whys, mid and cooldown breakdown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Snip Snip! is described twice as having a 'true-damage final snip'. It has no final snip — Riot's text is that Gwen 'deals true damage to units in the CENTER' on each of the six snips. Separately, nothing states what Fury of the Sands actually gives him.
audit.why: 'Final snip' tells a player to hold the cone out for a last tick; the real instruction is to line the centre line of the cone through him on every snip. And Fury of the Sands grants bonus Health, attack range, armour AND magic resist while reducing his Siphoning Strike cooldown — the armour and MR are exactly what your centre true damage ignores, which is why you fight him through his ult rather than waiting it out.
audit.corrected: 'Final snip' replaced with 'centre snip' throughout, and the R interaction stated.

audit.whatIsWrong: Siphoning Strike is treated purely as a stacking farm tool; nothing says it is an auto reset.
audit.why: It resets his attack, so his burst arrives on the wind-up rather than on a visible cast, and Fury of the Sands lowers its cooldown further — inside his ult the resets come much faster.
audit.corrected: Stated in Key Ability Interactions and the cooldown breakdown.

edits.after: Riftmaker/Nashor's plus anti-heal: your Q's %-max-HP magic and the true-damage centre snip melt his fat HP bar faster than Soul Eater lifesteal refills it.

edits.after: Riftmaker plus anti-heal lets your %-max-HP Q and the true-damage centre shred him faster than Soul Eater refills — your hardest all-in window.

edits.after: A fully-stacked Nasus out-scales you: Siphoning Strike one-shots and Fury of the Sands (120s) out-drains your healing — close before this.

edits.after: Land Wither (15s at rank 1) to gut your attack speed and kite, then walk you down

edits.before: This is where you take over. His only real threat is W Wither shutting off your attack speed and slowing you to a crawl, so bait it: let him commit, then drop Hallowed Mist as the cripple lands and you become untargetable while he flails in melee. At 6, Needlework slows him and your passive heals you off the damage you deal. Your Q's %-max-HP magic plus its true-damage final snip don't care about his armor — the fatter he builds, the harder you snip — so force extended duels inside your mist all the way to your first item.
edits.after: This is where you take over. His only real threat is Wither shutting off your attack speed, so bait it: let him commit, drop Hallowed Mist as the cripple lands, and you are untargetable while he flails — then you have fifteen seconds at rank 1 before it returns. At 6, Needlework slows him and your passive heals off the damage you deal. Fury of the Sands hands him bonus armour and MR, and the centre of Snip Snip! is true damage, so fight him THROUGH his ult rather than waiting it out. The fatter he builds, the harder you snip.

edits.before: Here's the honest part: a free-farmed Nasus out-scales even you. Once his Siphoning Strike is fully stacked it one-shots through a dropped mist, and his R health and Soul Eater sustain out-drain your healing, so the 2+ item window is his. Everything before that was your lane to win — you should have a CS and plate lead from shoving him off the wave, so trade that into objectives and end. If the game drifts to 30+ minutes even, his stacked Q wins the 1v1; don't let it get there.
edits.after: Here is the honest part: a free-farmed Nasus out-scales even you. Fully stacked, Siphoning Strike one-shots through a dropped mist, and inside Fury of the Sands its cooldown drops further while his Health and Soul Eater sustain out-drain your healing — the 2+ item window is his. Everything before that was your lane. You should have a CS and plate lead from shoving him off the wave, so trade it into objectives and end. If the game drifts to 30 minutes even, his stacked Q wins the 1v1.

edits.before: Track Nasus's Wither: His only kite. Mist it to deny the slow value. When it is down — Snip him in your mist.
edits.after: Wither (W, 15s at rank 1) is his only kite — bait it, mist the cripple, and you get fifteen full-attack-speed seconds.

edits.before: - Nasus Wither: matchup-defining — His only kite. Mist it to deny the slow value. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Wither (W): 15/14/13/12/11s — bait it and you own the next fifteen seconds. - Siphoning Strike is an AUTO RESET, so the wind-up is the tell, and his R shortens it. - Spirit Fire: a flat 12s. - Fury of the Sands: 120/100/80s.
